title: Choose Hackfind’s visual world
question: The roll assigned Check-in Wristband Rail. Keep it, take an alternate, re-roll, or take the category standard.

options.label: Check-in Wristband Rail
options.lineage: hackathon badge desks and colored entry wristbands
options.thesis: Your matches hang on the check-in rail — clipped, dated, ready to claim.
options.viewport: Hackfind as the desk mark; headline as the check-in line; CTA as Get band → Discover; a rail of synthetic matched badges with source + deadline.
options.risk: Reads as event merch if the rail doesn’t prove filtering.

raised.raise: How-it-works climbs as three visible check-in courses with sealed seams between them.
Signal color lives only on the wristband edge and CTA; the reading field stays calm.
A small honest match counter sits as desk chrome, not decoration.

options.label: Course Catalog Filter
options.lineage: campus registration catalogs and section filters
options.thesis: Hackathons as catalog sections — filter once, only your seats remain.
options.viewport: Brand as catalog masthead; filtered section list as the proof strip; CTA Enroll in Discover.
options.risk: Also the direction most student-tool runs land on — familiar and effective.

options.label: Wax Pack Match Cards
options.lineage: trading-card wax packs with stat backs
options.thesis: Crack the pack: each match is a card — face for the event, flip for deadline stats.
options.viewport: Deal three synthetic match cards on the bedspread; CTA opens the rest of the pack in Discover.
options.case: Holds clarity via stat backs; loses slightly on ID vs the hackathon-native wristband.
options.risk: Sports nostalgia can drown the product job.

options.label: Pulp Event Rack
options.thesis: Spin the rack — most spines stay quiet; your matches turn face-out.
options.viewport: One face-out matched hackathon cover with three-tier lines; CTA spins you into Discover.
options.case: Strong browsing ID; weaker on ‘never miss / accuracy’ vs a check-in claim.
options.risk: Lurid pulp energy fights sharp, accurate voice.

options.label: Safelight Darkroom
options.thesis: Your perfect match develops in the tray — timed, irreversible past the mark.
options.viewport: Amber field; a match print emerging; stations map discover → filter → remind.
options.case: Holds process clarity for how-it-works; weaker student ID.
options.risk: Mood photography can bury the CTA.

options.label: Coiled Earth Tower
options.case: Loses ID and clarity for a filter product; cream/terracotta is the category monoculture.

options.label: Iridescent Cloud Edge
options.case: Atmosphere without a product mechanism students can operate.
options.kept: Accent confined to a single edge band.

options.label: Minihompy Room
options.case: Decorating a room is not filtering hackathons.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: Clean student SaaS landing: hero, feature grid, soft accent — executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Centered headline, dual CTA, three identical feature cards.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other student tool by design.
